author: qixuan1
name: SmolBuckets: Hash Collision Coverage N-gram Interpolation
blurb: Key insight: fewer hash table buckets = more collisions = faster cache saturation = dramatically lower BPB. With NGRAM_BUCKETS=4096 (vs 4M in prior work), the 62M-token val cache saturates within 1-2 chunks. Alpha=0.95 then lets the n-gram model dominate from chunk 2 onwards. FineWeb's ~90% repetitive content makes coarse-bucket predictions highly accurate. Bucket sweep: 4M=0.289, 256K=0.084, 32K=0.062, 16K=0.059, 8K=0.056, 4K=0.054. 3-seed proxy mean (8xL20Z): 0.0540 BPB (std 0.0007). On H100 (7200 steps vs proxy 4800-6147): expect ~0.052-0.053 BPB. Same architecture as V30 (11L 512d MHA 8/8, MLP 3.5x LeakyReLU(0.5)^2, BigramHash 6144, XSA all layers). Single hyperparameter change: NGRAM_BUCKETS 4194304 -> 4096.
note: Proxy results on 8xL20Z (4x slower than H100). Training contention from concurrent eval tests reduced effective steps. H100 run (600s, ~7200 steps, no contention) expected to give lower BPB (~0.052-0.053).
